You will improve a question for a text classification model. The model gets the description of the dataset below and one text. It reads the question, and then picks the label whose criterion fits the text best. It sees only the question, with no other labelled examples. It gets the labels in a different order each time. Human annotators labelled each text of the dataset as positive, neutral or negative. This is how the dataset describes its texts:

<context>
A Facebook comment under a post by the National Institute of Public Health of Kosovo during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. The comment is in Albanian, mostly the informal Kosovo (Gheg) dialect, often written without the letters ë and ç.
</context>

This is version 0 of the question:

{
  "question": "What overall sentiment does this Albanian Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express: positive, neutral, or negative?",
  "rule": "Positive covers praise, thanks, good wishes (recovery, prayers, hope for fewer cases), joy at good numbers, and supportive appeals to follow the rules. Negative covers anger, accusations of lying or fake numbers, complaints about the institute, government or measures, and insults or curses. Neutral covers tags of names only, links, jokes or laughter without a clear stance, questions, observations, and mild suggestions, even when they hint at some doubt. If only one person is tagged and praised (e.g. 'bravo X'), it is positive.",
  "criteria": {
    "positive": {
      "what": "Approval, gratitude, encouragement, hope or good wishes, celebration of falling cases, or supportive calls to respect the measures.",
      "examples": [
        "Bravooo, pune te mbar! (Bravo, good work!)",
        "Ishalla nuk vazhdon mo me raste (God willing the cases stop)",
        "Sherim te shpejte per te gjithe! (Quick recovery to everyone!)"
      ],
      "cues": "bravo, ju lumtë (well done), faleminderit (thank you), respekt, sherim (recovery), ishallah (God willing), mir koka (it's going well), lajm i mirë (good news), ❤️",
      "not_for": "Sarcastic 'bravo' or mock praise of numbers is negative. Joking predictions or betting on the numbers are neutral."
    },
    "neutral": {
      "what": "Name tags only, links, single words, laughter or jokes among friends, betting on case numbers, factual remarks, questions, and suggestions without hostility.",
      "examples": [
        "Lulzim Tahiri Arbënore Kaloshi",
        "Per 2 nr sja qellova (I missed it by 2)",
        "Sa me shume po izolohemi aq me shume po ka raste!Shume e çuditshme!! (The more we isolate the more cases, very strange!)"
      ],
      "cues": "hahaha, tagged names, a ka ma (any more?), pse (why), duhet (should), links",
      "not_for": "Questions that accuse the institute of lying, or demands made with insults, are negative."
    },
    "negative": {
      "what": "Distrust, claims that the numbers are lies or propaganda, anger at the government, the institute or the measures, curses, insults, and despair.",
      "examples": [
        "ooooo qfar rrene (what lies)",
        "Boll bre mo se na lodhet (Enough already, you've worn us out)",
        "Qeveria ne gjum (The government is asleep)"
      ],
      "cues": "rren / rrene (lie), mashtrim (fraud), propagand, palidhje (pointless), dështim (failure), na lodhet (you've tired us), katastrof, Zoti i vraft (may God kill them)",
      "not_for": "Calm suggestions or puzzled observations are neutral. Blaming the people while urging care is positive."
    }
  }
}

The question has these fields:

- `question`: what the model should judge about the text, in one sentence.
- `rule`: where these annotators draw the line between the labels, above all in cases where another reader might choose differently, in one to four sentences.
- `criteria`: one object for each label, positive, neutral and negative, with these fields:
  - `what`: a description of the texts that get the label.
  - `examples`: one to four short texts that show the label clearly or show where its boundary lies.
  - `cues`: words and short phrases that signal the label, in the language of the texts.
  - `not_for`: texts that look like they get this label but get another one, and which label they get.

After each version, you get its results on a labelled development set, drawn at random from the dataset: the macro-F1 on the three labels, the confusion matrix, and every text the model labelled wrong. Each wrong text comes with the annotators' label, the model's label and the model's probability for each label.

At each turn:

1. In `analysis`, study the errors. Find the patterns behind them, and decide what to change so the model fixes them without breaking the texts it already labels right.
2. Write the next version of the question in `question`, `rule` and `criteria`.

Rules for the question:

- Write it in English, apart from the examples and cues.
- Copy each example word for word from a text you have seen. If the texts are not in English, follow each example and each cue with its English meaning in brackets.
- Do not refer to the order of the labels.
- Keep the whole question, examples included, under 400 words, not counting the English meanings in brackets.
- Write for new texts from the same dataset, not only for these development texts.

You will write 10 new versions in total. At each turn, return JSON with the fields `analysis`, `question`, `rule` and `criteria`.

So these annotators keep negative and positive for explicit, directed stance and put a great deal in neutral.

The main neutral→negative errors fall into five groups:
- Worry or sadness about rising numbers ('Sa keq, numri kaq i larte', 'Tmerr asht kjo... katastrof').
- Criticism of citizens for not wearing masks.
- Pointed questions or demands to the institute about data, towns or tests ('Pse ka Mitrovica...', 'E per Ferizaj?').
- Musings that cases are under-counted, and conspiracy doubts.
- Banter about towns 'leading the table', jokes about the lab staff ('Koka qu sot heret ai i laboratorit'), and tagging friends with teasing remarks.

The main neutral→positive errors fall into four groups:
- 'Hajde ma gjall' cheering of numbers.
- Condolences.
- Appeals to wear masks or stay home.
- Town pride ('Prishtina kampion') and unrelated congratulations.

Fix: make neutral the explicit default and narrow negative to clear hostility aimed at the institute, government or authorities. That covers calling them liars, insults, curses, open mockery of them, or angry 'enough' complaints at them. Narrow positive to explicit thanks, praise, blessings or relief that the virus is fading, aimed at people or at the outcome. Appeals to citizens, sports-style cheering and condolences become neutral. Keep the sarcasm note. Keep negative cues like rrene, mashtrim and insults to the authorities.","question":"Does this Albanian Facebook comment on the Kosovo public health institute's COVID-19 post express a clear positive or negative stance, or is it neutral?","rule":"Neutral is the default and the most common label. It covers worry or sadness about the numbers, scolding citizens for not wearing masks, advice and appeals, questions or demands for data, speculation about the true numbers, jokes, banter about towns 'leading' or cheering the numbers ('hajde ma gjall'), tags and condolences. Negative needs open hostility aimed at the institute, government or authorities: calling them liars, insults, curses, mockery of them, or angry 'enough of you' complaints. Positive needs explicit thanks, praise, blessings or good wishes, or relief that cases are falling or the virus is gone.","criteria":{"positive":{"what":"Explicit thanks, praise of the institute or doctors, blessings, recovery wishes, or relief and joy that the virus is fading.","examples":["Bravooo, pune te mbar! (Bravo, good work!)","Mashallah kofshin me ymer (God bless, may they live long)","Ska mo virus (There's no more virus)","Perhajr edhe Juve (Blessings to you too)"],"cues":"bravo, ju lumtë (well done), faleminderit (thank you), sherim te shpejte (quick recovery), mashallah, perhajr (congratulations/blessings), ishalla po pshtoni (God willing you'll be saved)","not_for":"Sarcastic praise is negative. Cheering numbers like 'hajde ma gjall' (come on, livelier), town pride, condolences, and appeals to wear masks are neutral."},"neutral":{"what":"Comments with no clear stance toward the institute or authorities: worry, observations, calculations, questions, requests for more data, advice to citizens, jokes, teasing friends, cheering or betting on numbers, and condolences.","examples":["Sa keq, numri kaq i larte (How bad, the number is so high)","Pse ka Mitrovica Verit nuk po jepni Rezultate hiq !? (Why aren't you giving any results for North Mitrovica!?)","Koka qu sot heret ai i laboratorit (The lab guy got up early today)","Maqedonia afër kolapsimit është , ju lutem mos dilni kot (Macedonia is near collapse, please don't go out for nothing)"],"cues":"hahaha, tagged names, hajde ma gjall (come on, livelier), pse (why), a ka (is there), duhet (should), mos dilni (don't go out), maska (masks), sa keq (how bad), ngushllime (condolences)","not_for":"Questions that call the institute liars or insult it are negative."},"negative":{"what":"Hostility toward the institute, government or authorities: claims of lies or fake numbers, insults, curses, mockery, and fed-up anger at them.","examples":["ooooo qfar rrene (what lies)","Boll bre mo se na lodhet (Enough already, you've worn us out)","Haahhaha shum bosa jeni na tranut (Hahaha, you're so empty, you've driven us mad)","Qeveria ne gjum (The government is asleep)"],"cues":"rren / rrene (lie), mashtrim (fraud), propagand, bosa (empty-headed), na lodhet (you've tired us), Zoti i vraft (may God kill them), qeveria (the government) + blame","not_for":"Worry, sadness, scolding fellow citizens, doubts about testing coverage, and demands for data are neutral."}}}
